html:
SMTO-LLM-0078 — The Gateway computer may be out of storage space for the model

GUID: cfa35dab-5f2e-57c8-9d64-f84be9a7084e
Slug: local-ai-disk-space-insufficient
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • While handling a model, the Gateway computer or its model server reported a storage-space problem. Part of a download may already be saved there.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to check how much free storage space it has where the model server keeps its models. SMTO only saw a message about space; someone on that computer needs to confirm it's really full.
  2. If space is low, free some up, for example by asking SMTO to remove a model you no longer need. Don't remove a model someone else is still using. Large models can need many gigabytes, and removing an unused one is the quickest safe way to make room.
  3. Ask SMTO to list the installed models on that Gateway to see whether part of the download is already there. A partly finished download may still take up space or need to be resumed.
  4. When there is enough space, ask SMTO to download the model again. With room to store it, the download can finish and the model can be used.

What success looks like

  • The download finishes and the model appears in the installed-models list for that Gateway.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't delete files from the model folder by hand while the model server is running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Local AI model operation hit ENOSPC on the Gateway, or the Ollama pull stream returned an error mentioning space; the latter is a text heuristic, not a measured disk-space finding.

What this means

  • The Gateway observed ENOSPC or the provider pull stream contained a space-related error marker; the latter is a heuristic and does not prove disk exhaustion by itself. A provider text marker is a lead, not a measured disk-space finding. Existing download effects still require inspection.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway observed ENOSPC or the provider pull stream contained a space-related error marker; the latter is a heuristic and does not prove disk exhaustion by itself.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the typed operating-system error with provider-reported text and free space on the model destination; inspect partial downloads before cleanup.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, check free space on the provider's model directory (for Ollama, its models path) and the Gateway artifact root with df or the platform equivalent, and confirm the error text in the provider log. Free or expand space without removing models in use, run local_ai.models to account for partial downloads, then request the pull again.
  • Have the Gateway operator confirm the storage cause and free or expand the intended destination safely; preserve unrelated models and reconcile partial downloads.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The destination has sufficient usable space and the explicit model operation completes with a matching inventory result.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • A provider text marker is a lead, not a measured disk-space finding. Existing download effects still require inspection.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
